newsitem.title: UK: UK prompt natgas softens as SAP falls, quiet later.
newsitem.headline: UK prompt natgas softens as SAP falls, quiet later.

text.p: The UK spot natural gas market saw prices fall in the prompt period on Tuesday as a system sell on the flexibility mechanism over the weekend put pressure on levels.
But there was virtually no trade in any other period and prices were largely unchanged in unusually thin circumstances.
There was a system sell on Saturday, a trader said, and this brought the System Average Price (SAP) down, so pulling prompt spot prices down as well.
"It's all SAP related," said one trader who had been involved in a deal at 11.10 pence a therm for Thursday and Friday.
Many were frustrated by the lack of trade.

One dealer who traded twice on the prompt market said "we tried to do other things, for example the April year, but with no success." He added that he had tried to trade the Q1/Q2 1998 strip as well but "we were getting nowhere."

Another trader said he was involved in administrative matters until mid-afternoon, but when he looked at the spot market he found "there was nothing out there. Prices today are very similar to last Thursday and Friday, but the whole market seems to have been at a standoff over the last couple of days," he added.

There was another index-related deal done in Q3 97, done on the basis of two indices minus a discount, with an absolute floor price established to protect the seller in the event of a significant price fall.
Tuesday's trade was for 100,000 therms a day, but the details were otherwise similar to a trade done on Thursday last week for 300,000 th/d.
Apart from this deal and the short-term activity, no deals were confirmed done, with few players seriously involved in a dull market.

The IPE was no busier, with no trade done yet again. Dealers put the lack of action on futures down to the lack of action on physical gas, and the net result was a market where little was done, and little interest shown, on any of the available trading tools.
